question: do short high-frequency phrases merge unrelated material into false formulae?

two_word_formulae_half_of_which_is_gramm.indra_is_excluded_and_the_exclusion_is_s: indra is the one content word above the line and its pairs are attested vocative formulae, not a word plus its grammar. Including it takes the recommendation from 59 to 97.
two_word_formulae_half_of_which_is_gramm.status: RECOMMENDATION ONLY. No formula was removed, and formula_nesting.jsonl carries all 4,825.

false_positives_inside_the_recommendatio: present and not hidden. pra mamhisthaya (RV/SV/AV) is genuinely from pra mamhisthaya gayata. That is why the list carries per-row evidence and is not a deletion.
did_short_phrases_merge_anything_here: no. The identity layer is exact string equality, which cannot over-merge. The near-parallel layer's shortest accepted pair has 20 characters on its shorter side and a median of 91, and the six weakest accepted pairs were read by hand and are all genuine. The only place a short phrase produced a weak claim is the 6 sub-threshold svaha identities, which are staged importable=false.
